Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

idea noun

a notion

also notion, I have no idea

classical

Cic. Top. 31: nōtiōnem appellō, quod Graecī tum ἔννοιαν tum πρόληψιν dīcunt (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. idea

nōtiō, nōtiōnis f.

noun, third declension

an idea of something, a notion, a concept

Cicero’s word for Greek ἔννοια: nōtiō virī bonī, the idea of a good man (Off. 3.81).

Other words

  • cōgitātiō, cōgitātiōnis f. — a thought, something that occurs to one

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.51: multō difficilior occurrit cōgitātiō, multō obscūrior, quālis animus in corpore sit

  • opīniō, opīniōnis f. — an idea that something is so, a belief, an impression

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 3.17: tantamque opīniōnem timōris praebuit, and gave such an impression of fear

  • cognitiō, cognitiōnis f. — a notion, an idea

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 154

    Properly “getting to know, knowledge”; in Cicero also the idea formed in the mind.

Examples

  • «quālem?» inquis. nesciō; tragoedia vocābātur

    “What sort?” you ask. I have no idea: it was called a tragedy.Plin. Ep. 7.4.2

  • quod in omnium animīs eōrum nōtiōnem inpressisset ipsa nātūra

    because nature herself had stamped an idea of them on every mindCic. N.D. 1.43

See also idea, know, believe.
